_comment: kaizen :: what kaizen knows about the Claude Code it is running inside. Versioned independently of the plugin, like the standards catalog, because the platform moves faster than kaizen releases. See docs/decisions/0010-doctor-diagnoses-the-platform.md.
_honesty_note: This registry is NOT an exhaustive list of everything Claude Code accepts — kaizen cannot know that, and a check built on the assumption that it does would start producing false errors the day a new key ships. So: a key kaizen does not recognise is reported as INFORMATIONAL, never as invalid. Only two things are ever reported as problems — a key on the deprecated list, and a structural fault kaizen can prove (a hook pointing at a file that does not exist).
_settings_keys_comment: Top-level settings.json keys kaizen recognises. Used to classify, not to validate.
_deprecated_comment: Keys that were valid and are not any more. Each carries what replaced it, so /kaizen:doctor can propose the migration rather than just complain. Empty is the honest state today: kaizen has not yet observed a settings key removed from Claude Code. Entries get added when one is, with a source.
_hook_events_comment: Every hook event name kaizen knows. Derived from the 29 event stubs the plugin used to ship, which were built from the Claude Code hooks documentation. A hooks.json naming an event outside this list is reported as informational — it may be newer than this registry — EXCEPT when it looks like a near-miss of a known name, which is almost always a typo that silently never fires.
_budget_comment: CLAUDE.md is loaded into every session, so its size is a recurring token cost rather than a one-off. The template itself asks the reader to keep it under ~200 lines; these are the thresholds /kaizen:doctor reports against.
_tools_comment: External programs kaizen uses, and what degrades when each is missing. `required: false` means kaizen still works, with the stated loss.

external_tools.name: git
external_tools.used_for: everything: detection, diffs, and the 3-way merge behind /kaizen:upgrade

external_tools.name: python3
external_tools.used_for: the standards catalog and workspace parsing; without it kaizen reads the JSON directly and cannot detect npm-style workspaces

external_tools.name: jq
external_tools.used_for: faster payload parsing in the generated hooks; they fall back to python3 then sed

external_tools.name: shasum
external_tools.used_for: the configuration lock; sha256sum or openssl are used instead when absent
